NKJV.2: Who walk to go down to Egypt, And have not asked My advice, To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, And to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
NKJV.3: Therefore the strength of Pharaoh Shall be your shame, And trust in the shadow of Egypt Shall be your humiliation.
NKJV.4: For his princes were at Zoan, And his ambassadors came to Hanes.

NASB.1: 'Woe to the rebellious children,' declares the LORD, 'Who execute a plan, but not Mine, And make an alliance, but not of My Spirit, In order to add sin to sin;
NASB.2: Who proceed down to Egypt Without consulting Me, To take refuge in the safety of Pharaoh And to seek shelter in the shadow of Egypt!
NASB.3: 'Therefore the safety of Pharaoh will be your shame And the shelter in the shadow of Egypt, your humiliation.
NASB.4: 'For their princes are at Zoan And their ambassadors arrive at Hanes.
NASB.5: 'Everyone will be ashamed because of a people who cannot profit them, [Who are] not for help or profit, but for shame and also for reproach.'
NASB.6: The oracle concerning the beasts of the Negev. Through a land of distress and anguish, From where [come] lioness and lion, viper and flying serpent, They carry their riches on the backs of young donkeys And their treasures on camels' humps, To a people who cannot profit [them];
NASB.7: Even Egypt, whose help is vain and empty. Therefore, I have called her 'Rahab who has been exterminated.'
NASB.8: Now go, write it on a tablet before them And inscribe it on a scroll, That it may serve in the time to come As a witness forever.
NASB.9: For this is a rebellious people, false sons, Sons who refuse to listen To the instruction of the LORD;
NASB.10: Who say to the seers, 'You must not see [visions']; And to the prophets, 'You must not prophesy to us what is right, Speak to us pleasant words, Prophesy illusions.
NASB.11: 'Get out of the way, turn aside from the path, Let us hear no more about the Holy One of Israel.'
NASB.12: Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel, 'Since you have rejected this word And have put your trust in oppression and guile, and have relied on them,
NASB.13: Therefore this iniquity will be to you Like a breach about to fall, A bulge in a high wall, Whose collapse comes suddenly in an instant,
NASB.14: Whose collapse is like the smashing of a potter's jar, So ruthlessly shattered That a sherd will not be found among its pieces To take fire from a hearth Or to scoop water from a cistern.'
NASB.15: For thus the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said, 'In repentance and rest you will be saved, In quietness and trust is your strength.' But you were not willing,
NASB.16: And you said, 'No, for we will flee on horses,' Therefore you shall flee! 'And we will ride on swift [horses],' Therefore those who pursue you shall be swift.
NASB.17: One thousand [will flee] at the threat of one [man]; You will flee at the threat of five, Until you are left as a flag on a mountain top And as a signal on a hill.
NASB.18: Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you, And therefore He waits on high to have compassion on you. For the LORD is a God of justice; How blessed are all those who long for Him.
NASB.19: O people in Zion, inhabitant in Jerusalem, you will weep no longer. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when He hears it, He will answer you.
NASB.20: Although the Lord has given you bread of privation and water of oppression, [He], your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, but your eyes will behold your Teacher.
NASB.21: Your ears will hear a word behind you, 'This is the way, walk in it,' whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
NASB.22: And you will defile your graven images overlaid with silver, and your molten images plated with gold. You will scatter them as an impure thing, [and] say to them, 'Be gone!'
NASB.23: Then He will give [you] rain for the seed which you will sow in the ground, and bread [from] the yield of the ground, and it will be rich and plenteous; on that day your livestock will graze in a roomy pasture.
NASB.24: Also the oxen and the donkeys which work the ground will eat salted fodder, which has been winnowed with shovel and fork.
NASB.25: On every lofty mountain and on every high hill there will be streams running with water on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
NASB.26: The light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times [brighter], like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the fracture of His people and heals the bruise He has inflicted.
NASB.27: Behold, the name of the LORD comes from a remote place; Burning is His anger and dense is [His] smoke; His lips are filled with indignation And His tongue is like a consuming fire;
NASB.28: His breath is like an overflowing torrent, Which reaches to the neck, To shake the nations back and forth in a sieve, And to [put] in the jaws of the peoples the bridle which leads to ruin.
NASB.29: You will have songs as in the night when you keep the festival, And gladness of heart as when one marches to [the sound of] the flute, To go to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
NASB.30: And the LORD will cause His voice of authority to be heard, And the descending of His arm to be seen in fierce anger, And [in] the flame of a consuming fire In cloudburst, downpour and hailstones.
NASB.31: For at the voice of the LORD Assyria will be terrified, [When] He strikes with the rod.
NASB.32: And every blow of the rod of punishment, Which the LORD will lay on him, Will be with [the music of] tambourines and lyres; And in battles, brandishing weapons, He will fight them.
NASB.33: For Topheth has long been ready, Indeed, it has been prepared for the king. He has made it deep and large, A pyre of fire with plenty of wood; The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of brimstone, sets it afire.

ESV.9: For they are a rebellious people, lying children, children unwilling to hear the instruction of the LORD;

AMP.1:
"Woe (judgment is coming) to the rebellious children," declares the LORD,
"Who carry out a plan, but not Mine,
And make an alliance [by pouring out a libation], but not of My Spirit,
In order to add sin to sin;
AMP.2:
Who proceed down to Egypt
Without consulting Me,
To take refuge in the stronghold of Pharaoh
And to take shelter in the shadow of Egypt!
AMP.3:
"Therefore the safety and protection of Pharaoh will be your shame
And the refuge in the shadow of Egypt, your humiliation and disgrace.
AMP.4:
"For his princes are at Zoan
And his ambassadors arrive at Hanes [in Egypt].
AMP.5:
"All will be ashamed because of a people (the Egyptians) who cannot benefit them,
Who are not a help or benefit, but a shame and also a disgrace."
AMP.6:
A [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning the beasts of the Negev (the South):
Through a land of trouble and anguish,
From where come lioness and lion, viper and [fiery] flying serpent,
They carry their riches on the shoulders of young donkeys
And their treasures on the humps of camels,
To a people (Egyptians) who cannot benefit them.
AMP.7:
For Egypt's help is worthless and good for nothing.
Therefore, I have called her
"Rahab Who Has Been Exterminated."
AMP.8:
Now, go, write it on a tablet before them
And inscribe it on a scroll,
So that it may serve in the time to come
As a witness [against them] forevermore.
AMP.9:
For this is a rebellious people, lying sons,
Sons who refuse to listen to
The law and instruction of the LORD;
AMP.10:
Who say to the seers, "You must not see visions from God";
And to the prophets, "You must not prophesy to us what is right!
Speak to us pleasant things and smooth words,
Prophesy [deceitful] illusions [that we will enjoy].
AMP.11:
"Get out of the [true] way, turn aside from the path [of God],
Stop bothering us with the Holy One of Israel."
AMP.12:
Therefore, the Holy One of Israel says this,
"Because you have refused and rejected this word [of Mine]
And have put your trust in oppression and guile, and have relied on them,
AMP.13:
Therefore this wickedness [this sin, this injustice, this wrongdoing] will be to you
Like a crack [in a wall] about to fall,
A bulge in a high wall,
Whose collapse comes suddenly in an instant,
AMP.14:
"Whose collapse is like the smashing of a potter's jar,
Crushed so savagely
that there cannot be found among its pieces a potsherd [large enough]
To take [coals of] fire from a fireplace,
Or to scoop water from a cistern."
AMP.15:
For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel has said this,
"In returning [to Me] and rest you shall be saved,
In quietness and confident trust is your strength."
But you were not willing,
AMP.16:
And you said, "No! We will flee on horses!"
Therefore you will flee [from your enemies]!
And [you said], "We will ride on swift horses!"
Therefore those who pursue you shall be swift.
AMP.17:
A thousand of you will flee at the threat of one man;
You will flee at the threat of five,
Until you are left like a flag on the top of a mountain,
And like a signal on a hill.
AMP.18:
Therefore the LORD waits [expectantly] and longs to be gracious to you,
And therefore He waits on high to have compassion on you.
For the LORD is a God of justice;
Blessed (happy, fortunate) are all those who long for Him [since He will never fail them].
AMP.19: O people in Zion, inhabitant in Jerusalem, you will weep no longer. He will most certainly be gracious to you at the sound of your cry for help; when He hears it, He will answer you.
AMP.20: Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of oppression, yet your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, but your eyes will [constantly] see your Teacher.
AMP.21: Your ears will hear a word behind you, "This is the way, walk in it," whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
AMP.22: And you will defile your carved images overlaid with silver, and your cast images plated with gold. You will scatter them like a bloodstained cloth, and will say to them, "Be gone!"
AMP.23: Then He will give you rain for the seed with which you sow the ground, and bread [grain] from the produce of the ground, and it will be rich and plentiful. In that day your livestock will graze in large and roomy pastures.

AMP.27:
Now look, the name of the LORD comes from far away,
Burning with His anger, and heavy with smoke;
His lips are full of indignation,
And His tongue is like a consuming fire.
AMP.28:
His breath is like an overflowing river,

For at the voice of the LORD the Assyrians will be terrified,

He has made it deep and wide,
A pit of fire with plenty of wood;

NLT.1:
“What sorrow awaits my rebellious children,”
says the LORD.
“You make plans that are contrary to mine.
You make alliances not directed by my Spirit,
thus piling up your sins.
NLT.2:
For without consulting me,
you have gone down to Egypt for help.
You have put your trust in Pharaoh’s protection.
You have tried to hide in his shade.
NLT.3:
But by trusting Pharaoh, you will be humiliated,
and by depending on him, you will be disgraced.
NLT.4:
For though his power extends to Zoan
and his officials have arrived in Hanes,
NLT.5:
all who trust in him will be ashamed.
He will not help you.
Instead, he will disgrace you.”
NLT.6:
This message came to me concerning the animals in the Negev: The caravan moves slowly
across the terrible desert to Egypt —
donkeys weighed down with riches
and camels loaded with treasure —
all to pay for Egypt’s protection.
They travel through the wilderness,
a place of lionesses and lions,
a place where vipers and poisonous snakes live.
All this, and Egypt will give you nothing in return.
NLT.7:
Egypt’s promises are worthless!
Therefore, I call her Rahab —
the Harmless Dragon.
NLT.8:
Now go and write down these words.
Write them in a book.
They will stand until the end of time
as a witness
NLT.9:
that these people are stubborn rebels
who refuse to pay attention to the LORD’s instructions.
NLT.10:
They tell the seers,
“Stop seeing visions!”
They tell the prophets,
“Don’t tell us what is right.
Tell us nice things.
Tell us lies.
NLT.11:
Forget all this gloom.
Get off your narrow path.
Stop telling us about your
‘Holy One of Israel.’”
NLT.12:
This is the reply of the Holy One of Israel: “Because you despise what I tell you
and trust instead in oppression and lies,
NLT.13:
calamity will come upon you suddenly —
like a bulging wall that bursts and falls.
In an instant it will collapse
and come crashing down.
NLT.14:
You will be smashed like a piece of pottery —
shattered so completely that
there won’t be a piece big enough
to carry coals from a fireplace
or a little water from the well.”
NLT.15:
This is what the Sovereign LORD,
the Holy One of Israel, says:
“Only in returning to me
and resting in me will you be saved.
In quietness and confidence is your strength.
But you would have none of it.
NLT.16:
You said, ‘No, we will get our help from Egypt.
They will give us swift horses for riding into battle.’
But the only swiftness you are going to see
is the swiftness of your enemies chasing you!
NLT.17:
One of them will chase a thousand of you.
Five of them will make all of you flee.
You will be left like a lonely flagpole on a hill
or a tattered banner on a distant mountaintop.”
NLT.18:
So the LORD must wait for you to come to him
so he can show you his love and compassion.
For the LORD is a faithful God.
Blessed are those who wait for his help.
NLT.19:
O people of Zion, who live in Jerusalem,
you will weep no more.
He will be gracious if you ask for help.
He will surely respond to the sound of your cries.
NLT.20:
Though the Lord gave you adversity for food
and suffering for drink,
he will still be with you to teach you.
You will see your teacher with your own eyes.
NLT.21:
Your own ears will hear him.
Right behind you a voice will say,
“This is the way you should go,”
whether to the right or to the left.
NLT.22:
Then you will destroy all your silver idols
and your precious gold images.
You will throw them out like filthy rags,
saying to them, “Good riddance!”
NLT.23: Then the LORD will bless you with rain at planting time. There will be wonderful harvests and plenty of pastureland for your livestock.
NLT.24: The oxen and donkeys that till the ground will eat good grain, its chaff blown away by the wind.
NLT.25: In that day, when your enemies are slaughtered and the towers fall, there will be streams of water flowing down every mountain and hill.
NLT.26: The moon will be as bright as the sun, and the sun will be seven times brighter — like the light of seven days in one! So it will be when the LORD begins to heal his people and cure the wounds he gave them.
NLT.27:
Look! The LORD is coming from far away,
burning with anger,
surrounded by thick, rising smoke.
His lips are filled with fury;
his words consume like fire.
NLT.28:
His hot breath pours out like a flood
up to the neck of his enemies.
He will sift out the proud nations for destruction.
He will bridle them and lead them away to ruin.
NLT.29:
But the people of God will sing a song of joy,
like the songs at the holy festivals.
You will be filled with joy,
as when a flutist leads a group of pilgrims
to Jerusalem, the mountain of the LORD —
to the Rock of Israel.
NLT.30:
And the LORD will make his majestic voice heard.
He will display the strength of his mighty arm.
It will descend with devouring flames,
with cloudbursts, thunderstorms, and huge hailstones.
NLT.31:
At the LORD’s command, the Assyrians will be shattered.
He will strike them down with his royal scepter.
NLT.32:
And as the LORD strikes them with his rod of punishment,
his people will celebrate with tambourines and harps.
Lifting his mighty arm, he will fight the Assyrians.
NLT.33:
Topheth — the place of burning —
has long been ready for the Assyrian king;
the pyre is piled high with wood.
The breath of the LORD, like fire from a volcano,
will set it ablaze.
